user.title: TONLY MTTL-W01 WiFi
user.description:
Where is the MTTL-W01 WiFi controller?

If you installed the MTTL-W01 WiFi app/add-on, leave this as the suggested address - it is read from the Supervisor rather than guessed. The strip itself is not configured here: the controller is the thing that talks to it.

The address is not your Home Assistant's own address unless the controller is running on the same host.

error.cannot_connect: No MTTL-W01 WiFi controller answered at that address. Check the app/add-on is running and that the address and port are right.

init.title: TONLY MTTL-W01 WiFi options
init.description: The controller caches its own readings, so polling faster than this gains nothing. Relay state echoes within 1-2 seconds, but the physical relay can take up to 20 seconds to close - so this is not a guarantee that power has arrived.

no_real_strip.title: No real MTTL-W01 strip is connected
no_real_strip.description:
The MTTL-W01 WiFi controller at {host} is answering, but only its built-in simulator is ({known}).

Simulator readings look exactly like real ones - four healthy sockets, reachable, settled - so the outlets are not being shown rather than being shown as fake. Switches will go unavailable until a real strip connects.

If you have a strip, provision it to call back to Home Assistant's LAN address and check that port 10086 is not blocked.

protection_unknown.title: Protection is configured for an unknown strip
protection_unknown.description:
Protection is set for: {devices}.

The controller has never seen a strip with that device id. Because protection is keyed by device id, an id with a typo in it protects NOTHING - so an outlet you believed was locked is in fact switchable.

Fix the device id in the app/add-on options, or remove the entry. Note that with no valid per-strip entry the controller falls back to its legacy global list, which is the safe direction.
